messages:
eva: heads-up from support: several customers in us-west-2 reporting 504 gateway timeouts and intermittent 502s around 14:12 UTC. They say failures line up with short bursts of high concurrency (100-300 reqs for ~30s).
frank: i'm seeing spikes in gateway logs: repeated upstream reset and 504 after 30s wait. Example: ```
[warn] 2026-07-11T14:12:25Z envoy upstream request timeout to 10.50.2.41:8080, route: /v1/embeddings, client: 18.205.4.3
```
gina: customer: cust_7741, route /v1/embeddings, model:redwood-neo-xlarge. Their SDK does retries which amplifies load. They reported latency jumps before errors.
infra-bot: autoscale-bot: KEDA ScaledObject "emb-svc-scaledobj" triggered at 14:11:58, 14:12:05; HPA shows desiredReplicas 8 but pods pending due to Unschedulable: insufficient gpu.alpha.kubernetes.io.
support-sre: tagging harish (oncall infra). can you confirm nodepool capacity?
harish: checking nodepool-autoscaler. Nodepool has autoscaler set to max=10, current=2. Cloud provider reports instances provisioning starting at 14:12:10, but nodes become Ready at ~14:13:50. Pod scheduling+image pull+warmup pushes readiness out to ~14:14:30. That yields 80-130s cold path.
eva: is warmup mainly model artifact download or initialization?
harish: both. redwood-neo-xlarge image pulls ~400MB of model shards at startup, then runtime does kv-cache restore and a short warmup generation to JIT kernels ~12-18s. On a fresh GPU node this is around 25-35s. Combined with provisioning that's why requests hit gateway timeout.
frank: i pulled a sample trace for a 504: gateway timed out at 30s waiting for backend. Backend logs show pod was in ContainerCreating state and never accepted connection.
gina: customer says their workload is bursty, not sustained. Historically they didn't trigger scale because minReplicas=0. KEDA scaler uses queue length metric with pollingInterval=30s and cooldownPeriod=300s. Polling too coarse for short spikes.
support-sre: proposed mitigations: 1) short term: increase ScaledObject minReplicaCount to 1 in prod for this route; 2) bump pollingInterval to 10s to detect bursts faster; 3) route-level change: raise gateway upstream timeout to 90s for affected customers until warm pool is implemented; 4) Offer a rollback/safer fallback model (smaller quantized model) for bursty requests.
frank: i recommend also adding a small pre-warmed replica pool on nodepool side (keep 1-2 idle GPUs) to avoid node provisioning. That would reduce end-to-end to ~30s.
harish: immediate actions: patched scaledobject in staging with minReplicaCount=1 and pollingInterval=10 for testing. kubectl patch command used: ```
kubectl -n inference patch scaledobject emb-svc-scaledobj --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicaCount","value":1},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/pollingInterval","value":10}]'
```
ops-jenkins: running canary load test: https://ci.internal/job/canary-emb-burst/123 - load generator fires 200 concurrent reqs for 45s to /v1/embeddings.
frank: after canary changes, observed reduced 5xx during small bursts. However larger bursts (sustained > 500 concurrent) still show capacity saturation; we'll need autoscaler tuning and nodepool buffer.
support-sre: customer communication: told them we applied a short-term change (minReplicaCount=1) and are monitoring. Suggested SDK retry-with-jitter config and offered to enable Dedicated capacity if they need hard SLA. Customer accepted temp measures.
gina: root cause summary so far: minReplicaCount=0 + coarse KEDA polling + node provisioning time + model warmup -> cold-start cascade and gateway 504s. Also note a config bug in scaledobject: metric name was "queue_length" but our prometheus exporter emits "inference_queue_len" for newer agents; some scaledobjects weren't matching causing delayed scaling in a couple of clusters.
harish: created ticket INFRA-824: fix prometheus metric name mapping in scaler to be backwards compatible. Also creating PR to bake top-5 models into container image to speed startup.
frank: temporary gateway tweak: raised upstream timeout for the route to 90s at 14:38 UTC to reduces immediate errors while we implement pre-warm. Config change: ```
# envoy route config snippet
route: \/v1/embeddings
  timeout: 90s
```
support-sre: next actions tracked: (a) harish to propose nodepool prewarm sizes + cost estimate, (b) gina to update customer and docs about burst patterns, (c) frank to add alert rule for scale-up latency and pending pods, (d) eva to own postmortem.
eva: alerts: add a pager when avg_scale_up_time > 45s AND 5xx_rate > 0.5% for 3m. Also dashboard panel for scaledobject trigger counts and pending pod age.
gina: repro steps for engineering: 1) set cluster gpu pool to min nodes=0, 2) run hey/k6 to fire 200 concurrent requests to /v1/embeddings for 30s, 3) watch scaledobject trigger, keda logs, kubectl get pods -w, and gateway logs. Example k6: ```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30s emb-burst-test.js
```
frank: note on mitigations: we should also add a graceful fallback in gateway that, upon backend NotReady, can route to a smaller fallback model with reduced latency. That will reduce customer-visible errors.
harish: i've scheduled a follow-up design meeting to define warm pool implementation and HPA/KEDA defaults (minReplicaCount >=1 for latency sensitive routes, pollingInterval <=10s, and nodepool buffer >=1). Meeting invite sent.
support-sre: closing the urgent escalation; keep thread open for follow-ups and postmortem. eva: i'll write the incident doc with timeline, impact numbers, config diffs, and recommended defaults.
gina: customer satisfied with short-term fixes and asked for ETA on pre-warm (3-6 hours for small pilot) and model bake (1-2 weeks).
ops-jenkins: canary pipeline shows steady state after changes; no more immediate 504s on burst tests.
eva: assigning postmortem owner: eva. please include cost tradeoffs for pre-warmed GPUs and fallback model rollout plan.
support-sre: thanks everyone — marking this incident as mitigated. :white_check_mark:
